title: Quotation, Ellipsis, and Emoji Triage Notebook
content:
Notes to self / quick triage for weird punctuation + emoji cases

Context and motivation:
- We keep seeing a bunch of realistic-but-messy user text in the customer corpora where annotation guidelines are ambiguous around quotes, multiple periods, and inline emoji. These are repeatedly causing low inter-annotator agreement and noisy model signal. This scratchpad is to capture proposed micro-rules, concrete examples, and a lightweight adjudication protocol for quick decisions.

Goals:
1) Normalize labeling decisions so that span boundaries are consistent (esp. B-/I- spans for named entities).
2) Keep rules simple enough for labelers to apply rapidly, but precise for adjudicators.
3) Flag unresolved patterns for follow-up tests and consensus meetings.

High-level principles (simple):
- Punctuation that is clearly part of the entity text (e.g., official product names with quotes) -> include inside span.
- Punctuation that is a structural or grammatical delimiter -> outside span.
- Ambiguous cases should prefer consistency with tokenization used by downstream model; if in doubt, split with note.

Key micro-rules (first pass):
1) Straight vs curly quotes: treat both as equivalent for labeling decisions. If entity is surrounded by quotes and the quotes are clearly marking the entity (e.g., She said "Redwood Pro"), include the inner text only (Redwood Pro) as the entity span; do NOT include the surrounding quotes unless the quotes are part of the canonical name (rare).
   - Example: She bought "Acme-2000" yesterday. -> entity = Acme-2000 (exclude quotes).
   - Example: The product's official name is “Clipper™” -> include Clipper™ (exclude outer curly quotes).

2) Mismatched or missing closing quote: if an opening quote appears with no closing partner in same sentence, treat quote char as separate token outside entity unless there is evidence the quote is part of name.
   - Example: "Headline from 3/2: Downtown store closes -> treat leading quote as outside. Tag the entity normally.

3) Ellipses vs repeated periods:
   - If three periods (...) are used as an intentional ellipsis (hesitation, truncation), treat them as outside entity spans.
   - Sequence of two or more periods used as formatting noise (e.g., "Price: 12......") -> collapse into a single punctuation token outside entities for labeling purposes, add tag comment.
   - If periods are part of an abbreviation (U.S.A., e.g.), keep them as part of token and include inside entity if entity contains abbreviation.

4) Trailing punctuation attached to entity tokens:
   - Trailing comma, period, semicolon immediately after an entity -> exclude from span (e.g., Acme Corp., -> entity = Acme Corp).
   - Trailing closing paren/bracket -> exclude unless it's part of name (rare).

5) Ellipsis used inside entity-like text (edge case):
   - If the ellipsis visibly replaces missing middle text inside a quoted product string (e.g., "Model 5...7"), treat as ambiguous: mark span to cover the visible tokens only (Model 5 and 7 are separate tokens), and add a comment to adjudication queue.

6) Emoji and emoticons (:) , :-), :P, etc.:
   - Standalone emoji that are clearly sentiment markers outside content -> outside entity spans.
   - Emoji that appear adjacent to entity tokens without whitespace (e.g., "Coffee☕House") -> treat as token boundary: labelers should split the emoji out as separate token; entity = CoffeeHouse (exclude emoji).
   - Emoji included in brand logos or product names (rare, e.g., "Snack😊App") -> include emoji inside span ONLY if the canonical name includes the emoji (confirm via quick web check). If not sure, flag for adjudication.

7) Emoticon-like punctuation (e.g., "... ;)" after a mention): always outside spans.

8) Inline code backticks and triple ticks: exclude formatting backticks from spans. If code identifier is the entity (e.g., `MyFunction()`), include the inner text (MyFunction()) but not the backticks.

Examples and label decisions (short):
- Good morning "Redwood" team -> entity: Redwood (exclude quotes)
- Check price at 3:00... -> entity: none for ellipsis; time = 3:00 (include 3:00), ellipsis outside
- Meet me at Coffee☕House at 7 -> entity: CoffeeHouse (exclude emoji), add note about visual tokenization
- "UNIX-based" systems -> entity: UNIX-based (include hyphen)
- We ❤️ Acme -> entity: Acme (exclude heart)
- Shop (beta) -> entity: Shop (exclude paren chars)

Adjudication and QA protocol (fast path):
- If labeler is >75% confident -> proceed. If low confidence or rule conflict -> add short note and file in JIRA-LAB-412 with screenshot/text snippet.
- Triage queue (weekly): reviewer takes the first 20 flagged items and produces a 1-paragraph rule clarifying the pattern.
- If pattern repeats across samples (>15 occurrences in a weekly sample), promote to a formal label rule and roll out as an update to the labeler checklist.

Labeler checklist (two-sentence):
1) Remove surrounding quotes unless they are part of the canonical name.
2) Exclude trailing punctuation; split emoji from word tokens unless emoji are known brand characters.

Open questions / edgecases to discuss in sync with Marco and SRE team:
- Compound cases where emoji sits in middle and appears to convey part of the brand (e.g. Shop🌟Now). How common is this in customer data? Need sample extraction.
- Ellipsis used as obfuscation (e.g., phone numbers masked as 555-...-1234) -> do we treat as partial sensitive PII and mark as redacted? Proposal: tag as partial-PII (special label) and exclude from training until we decide.
- Broken unicode quote sequences from legacy encodings (e.g., â€” " vs proper —) -> should be normalized before labeling; file a preproc ticket for converter.

Quick experiments to run (notes):
- Create a small 500-sample extract with high punctuation noise and compute inter-annotator agreement before/after applying these micro-rules. Expect IAA lift ~8–12% if rules are clear.
- Add a tokenization preview to the labeling UI showing how the model tokenizer would split quote/emoji boundaries; collect labeler feedback.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add a short page under Confluence summarizing the rules (linked in artifacts).
- [ ] Spike sample query for emoji-in-middle occurrences (Marco).
- [ ] Create small adjudication run with Zoe to validate the rules on 200 items (due 2026-03-01).

Random thoughts / heuristics (fast hacks):
- If a name appears on the web with emoji (brand uses emoji in official handle), add to canonical-name allowlist in the labeling tool.
- For speed, when in doubt on a single sample, prefer excluding punctuation and adding note; consistent exclusion helps models more than inconsistent inclusion.

Contact / channels:
- Slack: #labeling-ops, ping Marco Ruiz for triage.
- Adjudication ticket template: include snippet, tokenization view, rule applied, recommended change.

End of scratchpad. Will refine after Zoe run.

-- Aisha
